extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of comparative literature and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing poetry and prose with emphasis on national character, genre requirements (epic vs lyric), language, moral value, and the proper adaptation of foreign models. Draws examples from Spanish, Italian, and Portuguese literature to illustrate criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature can be much more easily contemplated and securely judged from the moral point of view — from which alone we can discover whether a literature be throughout national, and in harmony with the national weal and the national spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use moral evaluation to assess national harmony and the influence of literature; the author argues that on this basis Spanish literature fares well. This is an explicit evaluative lens to prefer when judging a nation's literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: National spirit and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Give weight to national spirit and influence rather than only to form and style: a literature's claim to value rests significantly on its penetration with and expression of the national feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form and style (e.g., Italian superiority in form) may be admitted, but national spirit and formative influence on the people count heavily when ranking literatures (examples: Spain favored over Italy on this ground).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language in unison with national character
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry (and literature) ought to be in perfect unison with the character and feeling of the nation that produces it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether tone, idiom, and thematic temper match the nation's character; Spanish poetry is held up as exemplary in being 'in perfect unison' with its people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid judging by foreign/classical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should not be absurdly judged by the rules of the ancients, of the Italians, or by the narrow decisions of the French taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should avoid applying an external, narrow standard wholesale; evaluate works on standards appropriate to their national and historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt foreign models with due regard for native language
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign influences (e.g., Italian style) may be introduced but must retain 'a due regard for the nature of the old language and poetry'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful borrowing keeps native linguistic and poetic characteristics intact (Garcilaso and Boscan are offered as positive examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic: unite historical truth and dignity with the marvellous
rubrics_metrics.description: The heroic (epic) poem should at all times unite historical truth and dignity with the free play of fancy in the regions of the marvellous; it matters little whether the ground-work be historical or fictitious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating epics, look for a balance between truthful/honourable representation and imaginative, marvellous invention (contrast Camoens and Ercilla examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic multiformity and richness
rubrics_metrics.description: An epic poet must be richer in every thing; he must be multiform; he must embrace a whole world of circumstances — the spirit of the past and of the present, of his nation and of nature; he must have command, not over one chord alone, but be master of the whole complicated instrument of feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value scope, variety, and the poet's ability to handle many modes and subjects; criticism of Tasso for uniformity versus praise of Camoens' multiformity illustrates this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of lyrical/idiyllic poets
rubrics_metrics.description: A lyrical and idyllic poet may show the happy condition of language and poetry in his country, but he can never bring either to their full perfection; lyrical poems are of too narrow limits and too confined import for this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize lyrical excellence but not expect lyricists alone to establish a nation's highest poetic standard — that role belongs to epic or dramatic poets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musicality of language and versification
rubrics_metrics.description: The charm of music in language and versification is a major poetic virtue (Tasso's language is noted as pouring forth 'the whole charm of music').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess poets for musical quality of diction and versification; musical poets often gain wide popularity (example: Tasso's popularity among Italians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for concetti/plays of thought in love poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Many fanciful thoughts (concetti) may not be perfectly just, but a poet of feeling and of love may well be pardoned such trifling errors; faults of this kind are tolerated in amatory poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate conceits within their genre context: such devices are more forgivable in lyrical/amatory works than in more serious epic writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and vividness of depiction (eye-witness detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid depiction and truth of detail — e.g., appearance of foreign countries, their inhabitants, campaigns and combats — that keep the reader aware the poet was an eye-witness are valuable poetic qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give extra credit to works showing first-hand detail and lively verisimilitude (Araucana of Ercilla is praised for this).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence as poem vs versified history
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware works that are essentially 'a versified book of travels and history of war' rather than a poem; an epic should be more than mere historical or travel narrative rendered in verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the work functions poetically (mythic/universal qualities, unity of imaginative purpose) rather than merely recording events in verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: National unity and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: A literature's preservation of a character of pure nationality and its continuity over time is a mark of value ('no literature has preserved a character of such pure nationality as that of the Spaniards').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the degree to which a national literature maintains a cohesive, continuous character across periods, resisting corrosive foreign or anti-national elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of diverse elements into harmonious whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry composed of many different elements (Portuguese invention, Provencal elegance, Arabic ardour, Italian art) that are not unlike or irreconcileable but form different tones of fancy and feeling whose union formed the perfection of harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the creative fusion of varied influences into an internally harmonious national literature rather than fragmented pastiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral, honourable, and religious tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Spanish literature is praised for being 'penetrated with the noblest natural feeling; strong, moral, and deeply religious' — nothing degrades thought, corrupts feeling, or estrange virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging works, consider their ethical tenor and whether they foster honour, principle, and faith rather than corrupt or degrade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid servile adherence to classical models (Virgilian form)
rubrics_metrics.description: The constant adherence to the Virgilian model was the chief fault of many epic poets of the age; servile imitation of form can confine a poet's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be critical of works that copy classical models rigidly at the expense of imaginative freedom and suitability to subject/mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of episodes and fragmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is in truth very little to be lost by throwing aside the connection of a poem as a whole; dividing a great poem into fragments (episodes) can supply a body of ballads or enhance enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that episodic structure or fragmentation may increase accessibility and allow outstanding parts to shine (Tasso's Jerusalem fragmented into popular episodes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose precision and the danger of Ahudeza (over-nicety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spanish prose attained fixed regular form and sharp precision; the danger is degenerating from extreme accuracy and acuteness into over-nicety, for which they have a precise name — Ahudeza.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for rigorous clarity in prose but avoid excessive pedantry or hyper-precision that undermines natural expression; Cervantes is offered as the model of balanced prose perfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate poetic richness into works of wit/prose fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: In works of wit the writer should be careful so to adorn with a rich effusion of poetry his narrative, machinery, and the whole of his language, as to preserve undegraded his title to the name of a poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prose fiction for its infusion of poetic qualities (Don Quixote praised for mixing mirth, seriousness, wit, and poetry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject choice should suit national/historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: A poet's subject chosen with felicity, fitting the spirit of his time and nation (e.g., the Crusades for Tasso), contributes to poetic success and patriotic inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a subject resonates with national/historical sentiment and provides material apt for the poet's aims (patriotic or cultural relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength and simplicity of diction as mark of authentic origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Old Castilian poems are distinguished by a strength and simplicity both of language and of feeling, which bear the sure marks of a very different origin (i.e., authenticity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize plain strength and heartfelt simplicity of expression as signs of authentic national poetry, especially in early periods free from excessive ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteral convention matters but no single universal rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The poetical language of Spain has not been subjected to any universal rule, excepting only that which regards the prevalent system of metre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect prevailing metrical systems as a guiding constraint, but recognize that overarching universal rules are inappropriate — allow historical/meteral flexibility.
